robots_txt_allowed.notes: The generic User-agent: * group allows these author-guideline pages, but robots.txt explicitly disallows several named AI-crawler user agents (including anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, GPTBot) site-wide. This scraper identifies as its own named bot, not as a browser or an AI-crawler UA.

peer_review_model.notes: single-anonymized is the default; We do not release referees' identities to authors or to other reviewers unless a referee voluntarily signs their comments to the authors. Some Nature-branded journals and Communications journals offer a double-anonymized peer review option. Please visit the journal website for information on the peer review options available.

preprint_policy.value: Nature Portfolio journals encourage posting of preprints of primary research manuscripts on preprint servers of the authors’ choice, authors’ or institutional websites, and open communications between researchers whether on community preprint servers or preprint commenting platforms.

ai_use_policy.value: Springer Nature supports the responsible and transparent use of artificial intelligence where it strengthens research quality, upholds editorial independence, and preserves the integrity of the scientific and scholarly record. AI is treated as a supporting technology. Scholarly judgement, accountability, and responsibility always remain human.

latex_accepted.notes: TeX/LaTeX: If you have prepared your paper using TeX/LaTeX, we will need to convert this to Word after acceptance, before your paper can be typeset. All textual material of the paper (including references, tables, figure captions, online methods, etc.) should be included as a single .tex file.

template_provided.notes: No general manuscript template. Nature provides a subject-specific ChemDraw template for chemical structures (http://www.nature.com/documents/nr-chemdraw-stylesheet.cds) and an annotated example of the summary paragraph (https://www.nature.com/documents/nature-summary-paragraph.pdf), but neither is a full manuscript template.

article_types.description: Articles are original reports whose conclusions represent a substantial advance in understanding of an important problem and have immediate, far-reaching implications.

total_word_limit.notes: Range reflects discipline, not a distinct article type: ~2,500 words for a 6-page article; ~4300 words for a 8-page article (physical sciences typically 6 pages, biological/clinical/social sciences typically 8).

figure_limits.notes: A 'modest' item occupies about a quarter of a page; 4 for a 6-page article, 5-6 for an 8-page article.

article_types.reference_style: References are each numbered, ordered sequentially as they appear in the text, tables, boxes, figure legends, Methods, Extended Data tables and Extended Data figure legends. When cited in the text, reference numbers are superscript, not in brackets unless they are likely to be confused with a superscript number.
required_statements: separate data and code availability statements
article_types.notes: Word/figure/reference limits are editorial guidelines, not hard caps; final length is at the editor's discretion.

article_types.reference_style: With links to citations; further citations allowed for fact-checking only.

article_types.description: Two-stage process: Stage 1 protocol (introduction, hypotheses, methods, analysis plan) is peer reviewed and can earn in-principle acceptance before data collection; Stage 2 is the full manuscript with results and discussion added.
article_types.notes: The guidelines page doesn't state distinct word/figure/reference limits -- Stage 2 manuscripts likely follow the standard Article formatting guide, but that's not confirmed on this page.

remarks: Scope limited to research-submission types (excludes staff-written content: News, Careers, Obituaries, Books & Arts, Futures, News & Views, Technology Features, Outlooks, Comment and World View). Peer review model, preprint policy, and AI-use policy sourced from https://www.nature.com/nature-research/editorial-policies/peer-review, https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/preprints-conference-proceedings, and https://www.nature.com/nature-portfolio/editorial-policies/ai respectively.
